reader.requirement: At --std 85 FUNCTION NUMVAL must return the numeric value its nonnumeric-literal or alphanumeric-data-item argument represents in either AR1 format (leading +/- or trailing +/-/CR/DB, spaces around each part, digits with an optional point or a leading point, at most 18 digits), with DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA swapping the decimal character.

edition-consulted.switches: ArgPredicate.AppliesAt for NUMVAL's CharacterCategory predicate (Since 85): the same argument screen at both editions

reader.edition-search: IntrinsicRenderer.cs has no Edition/Version reference; the digit cap passed to NumvalDec is keyed on the arithmetic mode (ArithmeticModes.NumvalDigitCap, 31 native), not on the edition; FlagConformancePass.Flag85.cs#FlagFunctionCall85 flags NUMVAL only under a >>FLAG-85 directive and does not change the value.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for conforming arguments: p2numval prints the same 19 lines at 85 and 2023. The digit cap is 31 at both editions, so an argument of 19-31 digits (outside 1985 AR2, whose result §1989:A.2.2 leaves undefined) is still evaluated at 85.

reader.notes: NUMVAL routes to the exact parse (NumvalDec over NvScan) in every arithmetic mode, so the value is the parsed significand at its parsed scale and no receiver or working scale can alter it. Every AR1 format variant probed returns the represented value. The refusal diagnostics cite §2023 clause numbers at --std 85, a citation-form issue outside this RV rule.

refuter.evidence: q4numval.cob at --std 85 (runs/q4numval-002): '  +  .5' -> 0.5; '123456789.123456789' (18 digits split) -> exact; '0012 CR' -> -12; PIC X(4) '7' -> 7; group ' -045' -> -45; NUMVAL(REVERSE("-21")) -> -12; NUMVAL("1.5")*2+0.25 -> 3.25; '-.000000001' -> -0.000000001; '5 DB' -> -5; '5 ' -> 5; IF NUMVAL("2.50") = 2.5 true. qanat.cob: NUMVAL(N"12") refused COBOL0900 at 85. q8nved.cob: NUMVAL of a numeric-edited item is refused COBOL1627 at 85; §1985 uses 'alphanumeric data item' as a category (VI-30, and IV reference modification 'numeric edited, alphabetic, or alphanumeric edited ... as if it were redefined as an alphanumeric data item'), so the category reading of AR1 holds and this is in any case the argument rule, not RV1. cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.29.4 RV1  (2.29.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1'; 'OK  §1989:A.2.29.3 AR1 ... the text is in AR1'.
